# Filters: the look over the whole picture

A post-process applied to the finished frame, after every scene has drawn and under everything on a CanvasLayer - so the show is filtered and the subtitles and panels are not. Filters COMBINE: each has its own 0..1 dial and they are all applied, in one pass, in the order below.

Filters - the look the whole picture is put through, after the scenes have drawn.

Scenes draw into one `SubViewport` that main presents through a single `TextureRect` at child index 0, with every panel and the karaoke overlay above it on their own CanvasLayers. A material on that rect is a post-process over the whole show and nothing else: no extra render target or pass, no change to a scene, and the UI stays legible. Subtitles are not filtered (grain over a karaoke line is hard to read, and a caption is not part of the photograph).

Filters combine, so this is a registry of amounts, not a picker: every entry has its own 0..1 dial and all are applied in one fragment shader in one pass. A filter at 0 is arithmetically a no-op, and when every filter is at 0 the material is removed from the rect, so the default show runs the code it always ran.

The registry order is the pipeline order, top to bottom, and cannot be read off the shader: the gate slip and the fisheye first (they move where the picture is read), then dots (they re-sample the picture, so anything after grades the dots), then the optics a lens adds, the grade, the emulsion, the frame. Monochrome before Noir makes the pair read as black-and-white noir, since Noir's split-tone is applied to whatever it is handed.

The fisheye moves the picture under everything that maps the frame to it: a click on the stage goes through `lens` (`Director.pick`), and a thing drawn into the stage that must read straight (the opening's title) is laid with `shaders/fisheye_straight.gdshader`, told the amount by its medium.

Adding a filter is a row of `REGISTRY`, a `u_<key>` uniform and a block in `shaders/stage_filter.gdshader`; the controls are built off the registry. A key with no matching uniform is a silent no-op in `set_shader_parameter`; the gate reads the shader source and fails on it.

Registry: `Filters.REGISTRY` in [src/show/filters.gd](../src/show/filters.gd) (9 entries), rendered by [shaders/stage_filter.gdshader](../shaders/stage_filter.gdshader). Select with `--filter key=amount,...` (or `--filter none`), or the Look rows in the Generative panel (persisted to `user://ghost.cfg`, `[director] filters`).

| # | Key | Name | Uniform | Default |
| - | --- | ---- | ------- | ------- |
| 1 | `slip` | Gate slip | `u_slip` | 0.45 |
| 2 | `fisheye` | Fisheye | `u_fisheye` | 0.45 |
| 3 | `pointillism` | Pointillism | `u_pointillism` | 0.35 |
| 4 | `bloom` | Bloom | `u_bloom` | 0.45 |
| 5 | `monochrome` | Monochrome | `u_monochrome` | 1.0 |
| 6 | `noir` | Film noir | `u_noir` | 0.55 |
| 7 | `static` | Static | `u_static` | 0.4 |
| 8 | `dust` | Dust & scratches | `u_dust` | 0.45 |
| 9 | `vignette` | Vignette | `u_vignette` | 0.45 |

## `slip` - Gate slip

Tearing: now and then a band of the picture jumps sideways for one frame and snaps back, the way a frame that does not seat squarely in a projector's gate is printed offset. The dial is how often and how far.

Uniform `u_slip`, default 0.45 when first switched on.

## `fisheye` - Fisheye

The picture as a fisheye lens takes it: the middle swells and the edges crowd in, so straight lines bow outward round the middle, while the corners stay put and the frame stays full. The subtitles and the opening's title stay straight over it. The dial is how wide the lens is.

Uniform `u_fisheye`, default 0.45 when first switched on.

## `pointillism` - Pointillism

The picture re-laid as overlapping dots of paint on a jittered lattice, each dot taking its color from where it sits and its size from how bright that is. The dial is the size of the dots, so a little is a canvas texture and a lot is a painting you have to stand back from.

Uniform `u_pointillism`, default 0.35 when first switched on.

## `bloom` - Bloom

Light bleeding out of the bright parts, the way it does through a lens. Only what is already brighter than the picture's own highlights blooms, so it lifts lamps, sparks and speculars without fogging the whole frame.

Uniform `u_bloom`, default 0.45 when first switched on.

## `monochrome` - Monochrome

Color taken out, weighted the way the eye weighs it rather than by averaging the channels - so a red and a green of the same brightness do not come out as the same gray.

Uniform `u_monochrome`, default 1.0 when first switched on.

## `noir` - Film noir

The hard grade: contrast pushed until the blacks close up and the highlights burn, with cold shadows against warm highlights. It grades whatever it is handed, so put Monochrome above it for black-and-white and leave it off for something closer to Technicolor.

Uniform `u_noir`, default 0.55 when first switched on.

## `static` - Static

Fine noise over the picture, strongest in the midtones and nearly absent in the blacks and the blown highlights, where the emulsion's own noise lives, and it moves at a film's frame rate.

Uniform `u_static`, default 0.4 when first switched on.

## `dust` - Dust & scratches

Dirt on the print: specks of dust (mostly dark, some light), the odd curled hair, and now and then a scratch down the frame that holds for a moment and wanders. It changes every film frame, the way dirt on a moving print does.

Uniform `u_dust`, default 0.45 when first switched on.

## `vignette` - Vignette

The corners fallen off, as a fast lens does wide open. Measured on the frame's own diagonal, so it is the same shape of falloff on a phone clip as on a widescreen render.

Uniform `u_vignette`, default 0.45 when first switched on.
